default._resident_note_1044:
**#1044 — the volume set's terrain shard: resident unmoved, and `ObjectStore` got 4 B *smaller*.** The set-upload session gained one field — `obc_app::SetUpload::terrain: bool`, the fact that decides whether the manifest this session will accept is `72 + 56 x N` or `72 + 56 x (N + 1)` — and the compile-time table moves **down**: `ble_object_store` 13,540 -> 13,536 and its `ble_total` 37,570 -> 37,566, the same 4 B seen twice.

The reason is a niche, and it is worth writing down because it is the opposite of what "added a field" predicts. `SetUpload` was `{ id: u16, shard_count: u8, committed: u32 }`: 8 B at align 4, with one **padding** byte and no invalid bit pattern anywhere, so `Option<SetUpload>` needed a separate discriminant word and cost 12. The new `bool` lands in that padding byte (the struct is still 8 B, measured) and a `bool` has 254 invalid values, so `Option<SetUpload>` now fits its own niche at **8 B**. `ObjectStore` holds exactly one, hence -4 B, counted once in `ble_object_store` and once in the `ble_total` that sums it. Nothing else in the table moved.

`.bss + .data` are unmoved at 295,808 B on the pinned host, `.uninit` at 118,432 B, the arena at 117,408 B, the poll frame at 9,728 B, the task body at 7,328 B and the residual stack at 77,280 B — the receive path adds no buffer of its own, and the manifest cross-check reuses `validate_committed_manifest`'s existing `#[inline(never)]` frame. `Armed` gained a `SetTerrain(TransferControl, Receiver)` variant, which is **narrower** than the `SetShard` variant that already set the enum's width, so neither `TRANSFER_ARM` moved. Flash is the `embedded` job's to re-pin as always: the pinned host links 1,357,880 B `default` and `ble` on this branch, against 1,355,528 B at the merge base — +2,352 B for the new object type, the `MS<id>.OBD` stream/commit path, the terrain record's commit-time cross-check and the session's clear-on-discard rule.

Symbols net +2,124; the sections moved +2,112, the 12 B difference being alignment padding the linker reclaimed. (The +2,134 / 22 B this note carried until the #1163 review round was an addition error in the prose, not a missing row: the seven rows above sum to +2,124, and the +2,112 section move is independently corroborated by resident 293,688 -> 295,800 and residual stack 79,400 -> 77,288.) `residual_stack` pays the same 2,112 B (79,400 → 77,288) because the bound is `_stack_start − __euninit`. `.uninit` and every arena figure are untouched — nothing here goes near the arena.

**The frames went the other way, and one of them was a caught regression.** `task_frame_measured` 6,912 → 7,328 and `boot_chain_measured_pinned_host` 28,116 → 25,700 (the SPI bring-up left the boot path). But the first cut of this PR made `sd::init` an `async fn`, because PR #1160 shipped `Semmc::start` as `async` — and awaiting that chain from `main` flattens its coroutine into `main`'s **task-body poll frame**, which is allocated in full on every poll forever: **6,912 → 13,376 B**, +6,464 B of permanent stack for a function that runs once at boot. This is the #677 / #1108 trap exactly, and `task_frame_limit` (8,192) is what caught it. `#[inline(never)]` does not fix it — it governs the future *constructor*, not the coroutine body (measured across four placements: 17,152 / 14,976 / 13,376 / 13,504). The fix is that bring-up is **synchronous** end to end: `Semmc::start` → `flpr_mux::bring_up_storage` → `sd::init`. Safe because the COM square wave the `async` shape was written to protect runs on the **P3 `InterruptExecutor`** (or, on `com-hw`, on TIMER + DPPI + GPIOTE) — it preempts thread mode rather than competing with it — and because bring-up runs before the ride loop, the BLE stack and the USB plane exist. It also makes PR #1160's "hold the mode across the entire `start().await`" contract structural: there is no yield left to hold across.

`boot_chain_ceiling` is deliberately **not** re-tightened from 29,696 to the new 25,700: it is a limit, not a record, and the drop is the SPI bring-up leaving rather than a budget being earned. `measured_flash` stays the `embedded` job's to re-pin, as always (the pinned host links 1,348,592 `default` / 1,348,584 `ble` on this branch).

The other two arms did **not** change and did not need to: nav (59,872 B) and USB (16,384 B) simply gained headroom, now ~57.5 KB and ~101 KB of free growth before either would cost a byte.

**The net, stated the way #1146 frames it.** The three arms used to sum to 168,576 B of permanent residency (render 92,320 + nav 59,872 + USB 16,384 — 168,572 B as the five donor `.bss` statics, the 4 B being `NavArm`'s padding, per P2's note); the arena costs `max(arms)` = 117,408 B — **51,168 B less even after the +25 KB spend**. Measured end to end against pre-P2 develop the figure is 51,296 B: total RAM footprint (`.bss + .data + .uninit`) 463,416 → 412,120 B, and the residual main stack 48,584 → 99,880 B — the same number arriving from the other side. **Both figures are correct and they are not the same identity** — they differ by 128 B, and every byte of the 128 has a name: P2 already carried a 40 B gap between its own two accountings (76,256 by max-of-arms against 76,296 linked — the arena's 8-alignment in `.uninit` plus `.bss` repadding); #1150's review round put 8 B *into* `App`; and #1143's cleaning took 96 B *out* of it. The end-to-end figure charges all three, the arms sum charges none. 40 − 8 + 96 = 128. The arms figure is what the *design* buys; the end-to-end figure is what the *linker* delivered. They corroborate each other to within named linker padding, which is the useful claim, not that they are one number.

Measured on the pinned local host, whose merge-base build reproduces this branch's merge base exactly (293,688 / 93,344 / 124,968 on both profiles — P2's figures less #1143's −96 B of `App`). `measured_flash` is unchanged by the caps and stays the `embedded` job's to re-pin. default._resident_note_1146: **#1146 P1 the render scratch leaves `App`: 462,376 → 462,392 B (+16).** A pure extraction, and the resident total is meant to be flat: `obc_render::MapRenderer` became `obc_render::RenderScratch` — pure per-frame working memory with an `unsafe fn init_zeroed` in-place constructor — and stopped living inside `App`. The board places it as its own `.bss` static, `RENDER_SCRATCH`, built where it sits (never by value: 92 KB through a return slot is the `RouteIndex::read_into` STKOF lesson) and threaded into `ride::run_app` beside `app`, the same way the `nav` statics are. The hash-insensitive writable-symbol diff has **exactly three** movers and nothing else: `APP` 136,560 → 44,240 (−**92,320**), `RENDER_SCRATCH` 0 → 92,320 (+92,320) — the identical block, relocated byte for byte — and `__embassy_main::POOL` 33,072 → 33,088 (+16), which is the whole increase: `run_app` is `#[inline(always)]` into main's task future, so the one extra `&mut RenderScratch` argument becomes a pointer-sized local in a frame that allocates every local at entry, and the arena rounds 4 B to 16. default._boot_chain_note_1108: **Boot-path stack gates, added after the #1108 STKOF (schema v2).** Every image built from develop between #1084 (EL7) and #1108 hard-faulted at boot — a stack overflow at `link::init_store`'s prologue — and NOTHING in CI went red. The gap: `poll_frame_limit` only measures `TaskStorage<F>::poll` symbols, but the embassy **main task's** frame is allocated in the out-of-line `____embassy_main_task_inner_function::{{closure}}`, which that match excludes. EL7 inlined a ~2 KB terrain-parse temporary into it (20,352 -> 22,400 B) completely unseen. Three gates now cover it. `task_frame_limit` and `residual_stack_min` are EXACT measurements. `boot_chain_ceiling` is a deliberately CONSERVATIVE over-approximation: the walk follows every direct `bl` edge whether or not the path is feasible (a `Mode::ReadOnly` `open_file_in_dir` monomorphization still references `alloc_cluster`/`update_fat`, so FAT-write frames a rescan can never execute are counted) and is blind to indirect calls, so it is a drift detector, NOT a stack-safety proof — the on-glass high-water in ARCHITECTURE_RESOURCE_BASELINE.md is that. `boot_chain_headroom_min` is the invariant tying the other two together: ceiling and residual are independently re-approvable numbers, and #1084 failed precisely because three individually-reasonable changes summed past the stack, so the combination needs its own gate. Validated against the bricked image: on 5de00ce the same code reports task frame 22,400 B and headroom -7,932 B (chain 56,532 vs residual 48,600), versus 20,352 B and +7,044 B on the fix. **Host spread, measured on this PR's own CI run ([30852527404](https://github.com/timohueser/OpenBikeComputer/actions/runs/30852527404)).** `boot_chain_measured` is TOOLCHAIN-SENSITIVE in a way the resident figures are not: CI's floating stable links a 35,356 B ceiling where the pinned host links 41,556 B — 6.2 KB of inlining difference, since the walk's depth depends on which callees survive as separate symbols. `boot_chain_ceiling` 43,008 B therefore sits above BOTH so neither host false-fails, which does mean its sensitivity differs per host (~7.6 KB of slack on CI, ~1.4 KB locally). That is acceptable because the ceiling is the fuzzy drift detector, not the sharp gate: `task_frame_measured` reads exactly 20,352 B on CI *and* on the pinned host, so `task_frame_limit` — the gate that actually catches the #1084 class — is host-independent. Re-pin both figures from an `embedded` run, not a laptop.

It is the same LLVM sinking decision, flipping back now that `ble::run`'s task no longer shares a module graph with the v1 USB planes.

  It is **not** re-pinned from that measurement. 9,728 is CI's and 9,664 was the host's on the same base, so the two differ by 64 B before this branch changes anything; writing a host figure into a row the `embedded` job gates is precisely the error c3a's review spent two rounds withdrawing. The gate is `poll_frame_limit` (12,288) and it is green either way. **CI re-pins this row**, and if it confirms the drop the 8.6 KB is a real reclaim of task-frame headroom rather than a number to celebrate here.

default._resident_note_1494_s6b:
**#1494 S6b — the board runs the pass: +568 B linked resident on both profiles, and **no ceiling raise is needed** — the row it would have been compared against was stale by ~15 KB.**

  **The delta is the measured part**, base (591ff816) and head built back to back on the pinned host: 304,832 -> 305,400 B linked resident, +568. **The absolutes below are CI's**, off this PR's own `embedded` run (the job `measurement.build_host` names as the authority): default 305,392 B / flash 1,463,112 B, ble 305,392 B / flash 1,463,112 B (the 8 B the two profiles used to differ by is gone with the drain), both with the guarded poll frame at 9,792 B, the largest task body at 1,100 B and 54,032 B of residual main stack. The pinned host links a stable 8 B more than CI, and it did on the base too — 304,832 vs 304,824 — so the two reconcile exactly.

  **`resident_ram_max` is deliberately left at 320,688.** The `measured_resident` row it guarded read 320,616, which is the FS8-era figure: FS7.5-c2/c3a/c3b took the real link down by ~15 KB and the row was never re-pinned (c3b's own note recorded 302,040 on CI). So the 72 B of headroom that figure implied never existed as a *constraint* — CI has ~15.3 KB of slack against the ceiling, and this slice's +568 B does not come close to it. Re-ratcheting the ceiling down to the true measurement is worth doing and is **not** this slice's to do: tightening a budget by 15 KB inside a protocol cutover would make one PR own two acceptance stories, and a branch already in flight against the old ceiling would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with it. **#1501 owns closing it**, and owns the other half the same drift produced: `deep_ride_high_water` (37,016 B, recorded 2026-08-20, row still says "delta rerun pending") was measured on the *old* ride loop — the very frame this slice rewrote — so the margin the guard computes is against a peak from a spine that no longer exists. #1494's scenario C reads the board's own `stack high-water N / M B` lines and produces the real figure; re-pin it from that run.

  **The per-symbol itemisation** (hash-insensitive writable-symbol diff of the two ELFs, same host, same toolchain). Five named symbols move and nothing else does:

  * `__embassy_main::POOL` 22,296 -> 22,896 (+600). This is the whole of the board's typed executor, `RideExec`, and it is inherent rather than incidental: the ride loop is `#[inline(always)]` into `__embassy_main`, so what lives between two `App::run_pass` calls lives in that task's storage. The four members that dominate it are the protocol's own shapes, each pinned by its own `size_of` tripwire — `OutcomeSlots` (<=224 B, dominated by `DfuOutcome`'s two fixed 32-byte version strings), `ExternalFacts` (<=224 B, dominated by `RouteUpload`'s commit-time sparkline), `EffectSlots` (<=160 B, dominated by `NavigatorEffect::Acquire`'s bounded `NavRequest`) and `DerivedNeeds` (<=64 B) — plus the in-flight removal's ticket and token, the planner's operation token and three flags. The 30 B `HostPass` struct it replaces is gone with the drain. **The 512 B derived polyline, the 128 B gesture batch and the `PassPlan` itself are not here**: they live in one lexical scope inside the store phase that closes before the next `.await`, which is worth 632 B of this task's future (measured: 306,096 -> 305,464 when that scope was tightened) and is the whole reason design point 9 keeps them on the stack.
  * `ride::CATALOG_STORE_REPLY` 0 -> 40. The reply slot `CatalogEffect::RemoveObject`'s round trip uses on the flat store's ticketed writer path. One slot per concurrently live call, and the catalog domain admits one operation at a time, so this is exactly one.
  * `flat_store::LIVE_TRANSFER` 0 -> 1. `CoreMode`'s transfer level at its source: the engine's own live transfer, published from `publish_upload` and read once per pass into `ExternalFacts::note_transfer` (S5 open question 2).
  * `flat_store::MENU_DELETES` 168 -> 104 (-64). The answerless queue keeps only the trip cascade; `MenuDelete::{Route, Ride}` moved to the answering `Request::RemoveObject`, because a full queue there drops the id and the domain's one catalog slot would never clear.
  * `flat_store::CATALOG_COMMITS` 4 -> 0. The commit-edge counter is gone: the store's own `FlatStore::sequence()` is the revision the fact reports, so nothing has to count edges to synthesise one. `CATALOG_WAKE` stays exactly as it was — it is a wake source, not a level.

  The five named rows sum to **+573 B**; the remaining **-5 B** is the linker repacking the anonymous `.L_MergedGlobals` blocks, which renumber wholesale across this change. Both figures are off the **same** ELF pair as the +568 section delta above — an itemisation taken from an earlier build of the branch would not reconcile, and this one does.

  **The physical consequence is measured, not assumed:** the residual main stack falls 54,592 -> 54,024 B on the pinned host (54,032 on CI) and still clears the 37,016 B deep-ride high-water by 17,016 B against an 8,704 B floor. `.uninit`, the arena and all four arms are unchanged to the byte, the guarded poll frame stays at 9,792 B, the compile-time allocation table matches on both profiles (in particular `app` is unchanged at 50,928 B — the bounded trip-member buffer #1491 would need is exactly what this slice declines to add), and `full_frame_sized_writable_count` stays 2.

  **Flash +16,860 B** on both profiles (pinned host, 1,449,352 -> 1,466,212; CI absolutes above), a record rather than a gate: `App::run_pass` and its fourteen stages are linked into the board image for the first time (40,086 B for `run_pass` itself), against the eighteen-arm drain and the 28 `apply_event` call sites that leave. The shared surface cannot be deleted while `LegacyLoop` and the tests still compile against it; S6c is where that lands.

default._flash_note_1505: **-5,464 B against #1494's pin, from asking the residual drain for three classes instead of eighteen.** `App::drain_residual_commands` walks `RESIDUAL_CLASSES` rather than `DRAIN_ORDER`, so the board's call site stops monomorphising the fifteen arms it then declined to perform. The saving is incidental \u2014 the change is a correctness fix (an intent admitted between two passes was being minted and dropped by that walk) \u2014 and flash is a record here, not a gate. Read from this branch's own `embedded` CI run; both profiles now link the same figure. Resident, `.uninit`, the arena, the poll frame, the task body and the residual stack are all unchanged from the #1494 table.
